Done. `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` all green (0 lint issues, full unit + integration + both E2E canaries passing).

## What changed

**One classifier instead of two.** `textutil.IsInjectedPrompt` (new leaf-package helper) is now the single source of truth. `strategy.FirstDisplayPrompt` and `compact.isCodexSystemContent` both delegate to it, so the drift that caused the gap can't recur. The prefix list is the union of both old lists plus the three shapes I measured: `<recommended_plugins>`, `<user_action>`, `<subagent_notification>`, `<turn_aborted>`, `<apps_instructions>`, `<plugins_instructions>`, and bare `# AGENTS.md`.

**The `<INSTRUCTIONS>` clause is anchored, not deleted.** No user item in 164 rollouts starts with `<INSTRUCTIONS>`, so I kept the original intent but made it `HasPrefix` + `Contains` instead of two unanchored `Contains` calls. `"why does the AGENTS.md instructions block get wrapped in <INSTRUCTIONS> tags?"` now stays a prompt — there's a test for exactly that.

**The JSONL branch got its fallback**, matching the extractor branch: an all-injected transcript keeps the raw preamble as its title rather than silently producing no `prompt.txt`, no title, and no warning. The return guard gained `|| meta.FirstPrompt != ""` so it doesn't fall through to the Gemini parser.

**Turn counts exclude injected items** via a shared `countUserTurns`, applied on all three paths (JSONL, native extractor, Gemini) — previously only one path filtered anything. I corrected the two tests that asserted the inflated count.

Also: dropped the pass-through `IsInjectedInstructionPrompt` wrapper, dropped the duplicate blank `codex` import in the test file, replaced the inaccurate "same filter the rewind display path applies" comment, and documented that `FirstDisplayPrompt` doesn't truncate.

## Verification

Rather than trust fixtures, I ran the code over all 164 real Codex rollouts in `~/.codex/sessions`:

| | Sessions titled with injected content |
|---|---|
| `main` (no filter) | 164 / 164 |
| branch as committed | 12 |
| with these fixes | **4** |

The remaining 4 have no genuine user prompt anywhere in the transcript (preamble + abort, or a review-tool result only), so the fallback title is the intended behaviour — not a leak.

Two new tests: `textutil` covers every real rollout shape plus six genuine prompts that mention the markers; `TestExtractTranscriptMetadata_JSONLOnlyInjectedPreamble` covers the JSONL degenerate case that had no coverage.

One thing worth noting: this is only the CLI defect from ENT-1653 — the ingest `firstMeaningfulLine` literal-first-line fallback and the namer decline are separate repos, and already-affected sessions still need the backfill the issue describes.
